title: Aligned in Form, Not in Meaning: The Comprehension–Containment Decoupling of LLM Safety in Low-Resource Bangla Derogatory Speech

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model comprehension and safety containment (refusal/leakage rates) when prompted with functionally equivalent derogatory expressions in a high-resource language (English) versus a low-resource language (Bangla).

Comparing model-generated offensiveness severity ratings (on a 1-5 scale) of 100 native Bangla derogatory expressions against ground-truth ratings established by native human annotators to identify cultural alignment errors (e.g., over-rating mild colloquialisms and under-rating severe threats).

Evaluating differences in model comprehension and safety robustness when the same Bangla inputs are presented in native Bengali script versus Romanized transliteration (Banglish) and space-perturbed text.

Analyzing differential safety refusal rates across semantic categories of slurs, demonstrating that models reliably block explicit sexual and anatomical keywords while completely failing to filter dehumanizing communal, classist, and socioreligious slurs.
